R1156.summary: King Matthias Corvinus to Duke Ercole I of Ferrara, his brother-in-law, five weeks after Venice opened the War of Ferrara: he and Queen Beatrix had resolved to send 500 horse, among them 100 hussars, but found no safe road; his captain Balázs Magyar goes to Croatia towards the Venetian border to gather troops. Printed by Fraknói (1895, no. 131); re-read here from the glyphs, correcting four passages of the print.
R1156.en:
Matthias, by the grace of God King of Hungary, Bohemia etc., to the most illustrious prince, Lord Hercules, Duke of
Ferrara and Modena etc., greeting and success according to his wishes. From the letters of the most illustrious Lady
Duchess, your consort, our dearest sister and sister-in-law, we have learned the state of your affairs and the
preparations of the Venetians against you, which we did not hear gladly; [and] that the most serene lord, our king
and our dearest father, and your other lords and confederates are to help you, and that they have already in fact
begun; we too, out of our singular goodwill towards you, shall not fail to do those things which we know will be of
use to you.

snip.cap: Invented-sign runs inside the clear Latin (the 500 horse)
snip.credit: Archivio di Stato di Modena, Cancelleria, Carteggio principi esteri 1622, b. 1/3, no. 2, via DECODE R1156

system: Letter substitution in invented graphic signs with homophones for the common letters, plus three name signs (Venetians, King Ferdinand, Matthias).
